title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Over a base scheme S, G = GL_2. ρ and σ are fixed regular semisimple elements; in the modular case of the next page, ρ = (0 1; -1 1) has order 6 and σ = (0 -1; 1 0) has order 4, the standard generators of SL_2(Z). T_ρ and T_σ are their centralizers, the 2-dimensional (generally non-split) tori {xρ+y invertible} and {tσ+u invertible}. From the explicit formulas on p.445, B'_0 is the mirabolic ('ax+b') subgroup of matrices with bottom row (0,1). G_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G×G×E' is the scheme of triples (α,β,μ) solving equation (82). Judging from (85), (82) has the shape [α,ρ] = [β,σ]·ε_1(μ−1), with [x,y] a commutator.

Aim. To give the general solution of (82), a piece of the 'équation des lacets' programme: equations satisfied by the images of the order-6 and order-4 generators of the modular group.

Theorem on this page. The morphism (86), (u,a,b) ↦ (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u), lands in G_{ρ,σ}. It is a monomorphism and induces an isomorphism (87): B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ ≅ G_{ρ,σ}.

Why it lands in G_{ρ,σ}. Since a centralizes ρ, the commutator [·,ρ] is invariant under right multiplication by T_ρ, and likewise for σ. So [u a^{-1},ρ] = [u,ρ] and [u b^{-1},σ] = [u,σ]. One is then reduced to the 'diagonal' section u ↦ (u,u,det u) of p.444 (85).

Inverse map. Given (α,β,μ) in G_{ρ,σ}:
- There are unique a ∈ T_ρ and b ∈ T_σ with αa and βb in B'_0, i.e. with bottom row (0,1).
- Uniqueness follows from (90): T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = T_σ ∩ B'_0 = {1}. This is direct: xρ+y has bottom row (−x, x+y), and this equals (0,1) only for x=0, y=1.
- Existence: right multiplication by T_ρ acts simply transitively on row vectors (c,d) on which the norm form c²+cd+d² is invertible. The next page gives a = (cρ+d)/(c²+cd+d²); the bottom row of α(cρ+d) is (0, c²+cd+d²).
- Equation (82) then forces αa = βb =: u, and μ = det u. Hence (α,β,μ) = (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u) uniquely, which is (89).

In modern terms: a global slice (mirabolic subgroup) for the free right action of the product of the two centralizer tori on the solution scheme of a twisted-commutator equation.
errors: The next page's (93) writes α a^{-1} = β b, which is inconsistent with this page's (88)/(89): α a = β b = u, α = u a^{-1}. One of the two is a notational slip.

Existence of a with αa ∈ B'_0 requires the norm c²+cd+d² of the bottom row of α to be invertible on S. This must come from (82) via the D-coefficient of αρα^{-1}, but it is not argued on this page. 'Mono, donc isomorphisme' is only justified given this surjectivity, which the text defers to (II).

ideas.what: Parametrization of the solution scheme of a twisted commutator equation in GL_2 as B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ, using the mirabolic subgroup as a slice for the action of the centralizer tori
ideas.modern_name: global section / trivialization of a torsor under centralizer tori; mirabolic slice
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard linear algebra over schemes; no specific attribution

ideas.what: T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = {1} and simple transitivity of a non-split torus on vectors of invertible norm, giving uniqueness and existence of the normalizing a, b
ideas.modern_name: free action of norm-torus on row vectors (Hecke/binary quadratic form normalization)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine computation inside Grothendieck's unpublished 'équation des lacets' notes. It gives an explicit global parametrization of solutions in GL_2 over a base scheme via the mirabolic subgroup and centralizer tori. It is correct up to minor slips and has no apparent novelty for specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '[-Elle-]' appears to be the crossed-out word 'Elle' with an editorial mark; the meaning is 'Elle prend ses valeurs dans G_{ρ,σ}'.
'il existe alors uniques solutions' is more likely 'il existe des uniques sections a de T_ρ, b de T_σ'. The handwriting reads 'sections' rather than 'solutions'.
'(α,β,μ) une solution de G_{ρ,σ}' is likely 'une section de G_{ρ,σ}'.
The final line is probably 'puis[que déjà] avant [...] d'explicitation dans (II)' or similar ('… already explicated in (II)'); the transcription is uncertain.
In (89) the handwriting shows corrections over 'u a^{-1}' and 'u b^{-1}', with 'det u' added above.
